dedupe_keys.name: topology informed recurrent survival model for water pipe failures

description: This Python workflow models recurrent water-distribution pipe failures with topology features and a Random Survival Forest. Its public repository supplies the entry script, graph-feature, embedding-alignment, gap-time preparation and survival-training modules, plus a synthetic Net3 demonstration input. The documented input combines pipe geometry from a GeoPackage, an EPANET Net3 network and pipe attributes with yearly synthetic failure indicators from 2007 through 2024. The model trains on recurrent gap-time intervals through 2019 and estimates each eligible pipe’s chance of at least one failure during the fixed 2020–2024 window. Its stated outputs include pipe-level predictions, survival curves, Harrell C-index, top-20-percent recall and permutation importance. A modeller could adapt this workflow to asset and break histories when assessing water-network maintenance strategies. The README says the source utility observations are confidential and the included numerical results are synthetic demonstrations, not measured real-world accuracy. It names output folders and two capitalized script paths absent from the inspected tree; the top-level run script was not executed. BSD-3-Clause is stated for the repository, while the Net3 example has upstream EPANET attribution. This supports risk-based maintenance planning and resilience simulations, but measured local histories are needed for real calibration.
